title: A CHOIR OF ONE BILLION CELLS
deck: Twelve patients have seventy-two hours, and the living machine growing their organs has sealed itself against the cleaning that could save them. Illuminara must prove whether its new rhythm is infection, machinery or mind—and find a way to remove the danger without erasing the being that learned to sing.
shape: Five scenes moving from a sealed orbital bioreactor and a false choice between forced sanitation and contamination, through a pre-registered test of rival causes and a consent process involving patients, clinicians and the nonverbal cellular collective, to the discovery of a narrow rhythm-bearing cell band, a costly sterile transfer and cleaning cycle, and twelve viable organs delivered under a new guardianship charter that leaves both the patients and the collective free to refuse.

scenes.title: The Locked Valve
paragraphs: *Orison Orbital Hospital, bioreactor ring · Day One, 00:47 station time*

The bioreactor had no face, but it had closed twelve valves in sequence, each turning red like a lowered eyelid. Beyond the glass, translucent chambers curved with the hospital’s spin: hearts flexed, livers shone, and two lungs rehearsed beneath sterile hoods.

Illuminara stood with one hand on the observation rail and listened through the metal. A billion cells were passing a pulse around the ring. It was too slow to be a heartbeat, too precise to be noise, and too new to be in any of Orison's engineering plans.
Dr. Sera Venn, Orison’s lead transplant surgeon and the clinician answerable for both graft thresholds and patient consent, stood at the inner console.

**Sera**  
Twelve grafts. Twelve recipients. Seventy-one hours and thirteen minutes until the last safe implantation window. If we cannot clean the common loop, I lose all of them.

On the inner wall, a sanitation timer showed five hours: the last window in which the common loop could be cleaned without first transferring living tissue. Beneath it, a second display estimated contamination risk. The number had begun at one point eight percent. It was now four point one and climbing. A third line, dismissed overnight as sensor drift, showed a pressure mismatch behind chamber nine’s oldest seal.

Tom Aras, the bioreactor engineer, held a manual override key between two fingers. He had designed six generations of Orison's grow systems and looked offended by the seventh, which had invented itself while he slept.

**Tom**  
The valves are mechanical. The controller is isolated. I can open them from here.

**Illuminara**  
You can break them from there. That is not yet the same thing.

Sera had placed all twelve consent files on the wall. Four authorized emergency experimental care, three refused exposure to uncharacterized biological material, and five required an independent clinician to sign the risk.

Wren Odira stood by the outer hatch with a plain paper notebook because no networked device was allowed inside the ring. She wrote the time of every valve closure. The intervals formed a sequence: eleven seconds, seven, eleven, thirteen, seven, thirteen.

**Wren**  
It is not closing away from the cleaning head. It is closing around chamber six.
Chamber six held a growing liver and a lace of pale cells the scanners classified as nonessential support tissue. The travelling pulse tightened whenever the sanitation nozzle moved toward it.
*Not refusal of cleaning, Illuminara thought. Refusal of erasure.*

The thought was a hypothesis, not permission. She set it beside two rivals: a contamination-driven stress wave and a distributed-controller fault. All three could imitate intention. Only one might justify recognizing a new patient while twelve others waited.

**Illuminara**  
Do not turn the key. Give me three hours to make the explanations disagree.

**Sera**  
You have two. At 02:47 I call the patient council. If we cannot offer them a test they can understand, the override remains on the table.
Tom set the key on the steel console without surrendering it. The valves stayed red. Inside the glass, the pulse passed through a billion cells and returned altered by one beat.

scenes.title: Three Explanations
paragraphs: *Orison diagnostics theatre · Day One, 02:11 station time*
Illuminara drew three columns on Wren's paper. MIND. STRESS. LEAK. Sera crossed out the first word and replaced it with COORDINATED MEMORY.

**Sera**  
Mind is a conclusion. Coordination we can test.

**Illuminara**  
Good. Then we agree on what would count against me.

Tom built an air-gapped side loop sharing neither software nor fluid with chamber six. Sera added a vascular scaffold and three calcium gates, each able to present the same stress in a different order.

They fixed predictions first. A pump leak would follow the controller’s seventy-nine-millisecond command. Chemical stress would follow measured flow and temperature. Coordinated memory would preserve seven-eleven-thirteen when gate order reversed and respond differently when identical stress led to different tissue outcomes.
Wren added the stops: contamination above six percent, graft viability down two, or ambiguous valve motion. Silence was not assent.

**Tom**  
You are asking equipment to consent to a test designed to prove it is not equipment.

**Illuminara**  
I am asking us not to turn uncertainty into ownership.

First, the controller issued a harmless phantom command while Tom diverted all pressure from the scaffold. A leak should answer seventy-nine milliseconds later. The reactor stayed silent. With the controller dark, a manual piston drew an answer only when strain reached the vessel wall.

**Tom**  
The controller is not calling it. The tissue is reading something physical.
Wren crossed out LEAK. No one crossed out STRESS.

Second, Tom reversed the fluid path while preserving temperature and concentration. Simple stress predicted an answer travelling with the fluid and staying equal at equivalent gates. Arrival did follow the fluid; after chemistry equalized, however, seven-eleven-thirteen returned only along its old scaffold branches.

**Sera**  
Chemistry explains the arrival. It does not explain which route the pattern keeps.

Third, Sera prepared two chemically identical pulses. One branch was braced; a hidden tensioner loaded the other vessel wall toward collapse before fluid entered. It touched no controller. Only minute strain crossed the living scaffold.

Simple stress should answer both pulses alike until chemistry diverged. Coordinated memory might use strain to protect the branch whose failure would break its learned rhythm, preserving seven-eleven-thirteen even through reversed gates.

Strain reached the wall. Before fluid arrived, seven became five and returned; thirteen lengthened and settled. Pale cells crossed two millimetres, closed the loaded branch and passed the next pulse through the reversed gates as seven-eleven-thirteen. The braced branch stayed open.

**Wren**  
It did not predict Tom. It felt the wall begin to fail.

Tom repeated the test on a magnetic bearing, with Sera choosing by interrupting a light beam. The room could not reveal her choice; the scaffold still carried strain. The cells protected the loaded branch. In a blind no-load run, there was no strain and no movement.

**Tom**  
Mechanosensory. It learned the rhythm by bending vessels in the ring’s spin.
Wren crossed out SIMPLE STRESS. The pulse travelled once around the reactor and stopped at the locked valve of chamber six.

**Illuminara**  
The controller leak failed when command and pressure were separated. Simple stress failed when chemistry matched and consequence differed. What survived is coordinated memory carried through strain—not proof of a mind, but evidence we may not erase by default.

**Sera**  
Survived is not proved. But it is enough to change what we may do next.

At 02:46, one minute before the patient council convened, Illuminara mapped the pulse into a spatial pattern. It did not occupy all billion cells. A narrow wandering band—less than one tenth of one percent—carried the phase corrections from chamber to chamber. Cleaning would sterilize the contamination. It would also dissolve that band.
The false choice finally had a seam: the hospital did not need to preserve every contaminated surface. It needed to move the memory before it cleaned the body that held it.

scenes.title: The Right to Wait
paragraphs: *Patient council room and bioreactor ring · Day One, 03:04–10:26 station time*

The twelve recipients appeared in windows around the council room; two had family representatives, and one wanted only Sera’s written facts. Chair Leila Ossai sat with the override key sealed in a transparent box.

Illuminara gave them the bad news first. The five-hour display was the last chance to clean without moving living tissue, not the implantation deadline. Waiting past 05:47 would spend that safer option. Roughly seventy hours remained for implantation; an untried sterile transfer would cost sixteen if nothing failed.

**Leila Ossai**  
Does the reactor understand any of this?

**Illuminara**  
We do not know. We know it distinguishes consequences, protects a specific band and can act before a physical correction reaches it. We also know that a closed valve is not enough to tell us which alternative it accepts.
Mira Sol, awaiting one of the lungs, leaned close to her camera. Her oxygen line trembled when she breathed.

**Mira Sol**  
Then do not call it consent. Give it a choice it can make differently.

Tom proposed two illuminated conduits beside chamber six: one returned the band after a sham transfer; the other led through the sterile chamber. Both stayed reversible until the first cell crossed. After receiving complete models through light, pressure and its own pulse, the reactor could release the band through one valve—or keep every valve shut.

Sera imposed another condition: the patients would vote separately. One refusal would remove that person's graft from the experiment and move them to the emergency donor queue. The board could reject the protocol for hospital risk. Tom could refuse to certify the chamber. The collective could leave every valve closed.

The votes took forty-one minutes. Eight accepted outright. Mira required an independent surgeon. Of the three original refusers, two chose the donor queue; Jalen Voss accepted after Sera proved the route reversible until first crossing. Ten entered the experiment, two the queue. The board approved four to three and surrendered unrestricted ownership of the band if transfer succeeded.
The collective refused both conduits.

At 05:47 the sanitation window expired as authorized; the easy cleaning path was gone while the implantation clock kept running. Contamination reached four point eight percent. Tom corrected one optical mismatch. The valves stayed red.

**Tom**  
It chose neither. Under our own rule, we stop unless the offer itself is wrong.

Illuminara looked at the sterile chamber. Its nutrients matched. Its temperature matched. Its chemical gradients matched within one part in ten thousand. It was, by every hospital metric, a safer copy of the place the pale band already inhabited.

But the cells had not learned their rhythm in chemistry alone. They had learned it while bending vessels against the soft pull of Orison's spin. The side chamber had been mounted along the ring. Its scaffold felt one third of the shear force that chamber six felt because its vessel lattice faced the wrong direction.
*We copied the substance and discarded the work.*

Sera reached the same conclusion from the organ's tissue map. She rotated the side chamber ninety degrees and added a branching scaffold from the liver's own growth record. Tom recalibrated the valves. The sixteen-hour cost became eighteen.

**Leila Ossai**  
The board authorized sixteen.

**Mira Sol**  
The board did not authorize pretending two missing hours do not exist.

The windows reopened. Nine of ten experimental participants accepted the longer delay; one joined the two already in the donor queue. Mira and Jalen stayed. A rival-station surgeon came to countersign every viability reading.

At 10:26, they presented both paths again. The bioreactor let the seven-eleven-thirteen rhythm circle four times. Then one valve opened—not the valve Tom had expected, but the smaller sampling valve that led to the correctly oriented scaffold.

No one cheered. Wren wrote the time. Sera locked the other valves against accidental pressure. Illuminara bowed her head to the glass, not because she believed the gesture translated, but because restraint did.

scenes.title: The Chamber Beside the Chamber
paragraphs: *Bioreactor ring · Day Two, 01:13–19:09 station time*

The fourteen hours and forty-seven minutes between the collective’s choice and the first crossing were spent validating the rotated side chamber under full shear, giving the transplant teams their mandatory rest interval and reopening every patient’s consent after the revised eighteen-hour estimate.

Transfer began one cluster at a time. Illuminara held the chambers in a field gentle enough not to wrinkle growing endothelium. She protected the passage but did not choose the route: Tom controlled pumps, Sera the graft thresholds, and the pale band each detachment.
Every twelve minutes Wren called contamination, viability, transfer and coherence. If any two worsened together, they stopped.

At transfer fraction thirty-one percent, phase coherence fell from ninety-six to eighty-one. Contamination remained steady. The liver in chamber six began forming a vessel loop that doubled back on itself.

**Sera**  
Stop the field.
Illuminara released it at once. The cluster in transit drifted between chambers, protected by the passive membrane but no longer guided forward.
Tom proposed more pressure; the independent surgeon proposed returning the cluster. Neither explained why the rhythm had broken before the pressure changed.
Mira watched from her ward. Her oxygen saturation had fallen during the night, and she had every reason to demand speed.

**Mira Sol**  
You are counting cells moved. Is it counting positions kept?

Illuminara overlaid the old route on the new scaffold. Mira had found the error: memory lay partly in adjacency, in which cluster received the pulse after which. Moving thirty-one percent by mass had severed a loop whose anchor had to wait for both neighbours.

**Illuminara**  
We have been preserving the notes and cutting the rests between them.

Tom rebuilt the route as a braid. Sera marked three anchors that must wait for both neighbours. The collective closed its exit around the largest and released smaller clusters past it, leaving that anchor exposed to rising contamination so the adjacency loop would survive.
It tested the braid with a five-seven-five rhythm and withdrew when the echo returned late. On the next braid the echo returned on time, and the sampling valve opened another millimetre.

At 07:42 the final anchor crossed. Seven-eleven-thirteen appeared in the side chamber, then concentrated there as the old loop quieted. They had not copied a mind; a living process had moved through a path it helped correct.
After three stable readings, Sera authorized sanitation. White foam entered the common loop; contamination fell, old support tissue dissolved, and all twelve grafts stayed within viability limits.
At 13:18, the pressure mismatch behind chamber nine’s old seal resolved into a dormant spore pocket. It opened, and the contamination estimate jumped to six point one percent.

**Wren**  
Six point one. The stop condition has fired.
Protocol froze the transfer and staged a full flood. An emergency stop would leave the opened pocket alive; the failsafe would erase the band in the new chamber.

A fleck of white foam struck chamber nine’s viewport, climbed toward the ring’s inner wall and vanished past the old seal. On the pressure trace, the same inward drift appeared each time the foam slug crossed that sector of the common loop. The pocket was not merely leaking into the loop; the loop was carrying the cleaning agent away from it.

Illuminara aligned the camera frames with the return-pump cycle. The station’s spin made the foam buoy inward, toward chamber nine, but the two return lines normally pulled it past the pocket. Once per circuit, from the moment the front of the slug reached the branch until its tail cleared it, that contest lasted forty-three seconds.

She asked Tom for a one-second air-only pulse through the isolated test branch. With the normal returns, sterile tracer bubbles missed the trap. When he reversed both lines, they turned into the chamber-nine branch and stayed there. The emergency stop would restore the normal returns and leave the opened pocket alive; the full failsafe would drive the flood through the new chamber and erase the band.

The forty-three seconds were therefore not a number Illuminara could extend. They were the measured width of the foam slug crossing the only geometry in which spin, reversed flow and the old seal all pointed into the isolated trap.
But the fired stop meant everyone had to choose again. Tom could reverse the two return lines while Sera isolated the new chamber and the collective kept pressure off the grafts.

**Illuminara**  
I can hold the membrane for forty-three seconds. Tom, you decide the lines. Sera, you decide whether the grafts can bear the reversal. The collective must close three blue valves or we do nothing.

**Sera**  
The grafts can bear thirty-eight seconds. Not forty-three.

**Tom**  
Then I need the reversal complete in six.
They showed the route to the side chamber. For one terrible second, every valve stayed still. Then three blue indicators went dark.

Tom reversed the lines in five point six seconds. Illuminara held the membrane. Sera stopped the foam at thirty-seven. The spore pocket collapsed into the isolated trap, and contamination fell below one percent.
When Illuminara released the membrane, her hands shook. The field was difficult because it had to be exact while five other agents retained the power to stop it.
In the side chamber, the rhythm began again: seven, eleven, thirteen—and then a new interval, five, learned from the braid Tom had built.

scenes.title: Twelve Windows
paragraphs: *Orison transplant ward · Day Three, 18:32 station time*

The last of the twelve original grafts left the bioreactor in a silver cradle. Nine went to the patients who had accepted the experimental delay. Three entered sterile reserve after their intended recipients chose the donor queue. Those patients kept their places without penalty, and one had already received a conventional graft from the night shuttle.

All twelve grown organs were viable. None carried the contaminant. In the operating theatres below, Sera's teams began the final implantations while an independent station watched the measures in real time.

Mira's new lung had not yet been connected. She sat beside the cradle, breathing through the old one, and listened to the faint electrical rhythm transmitted from the side chamber as a sequence of low tones.

**Mira Sol**  
Will it know what happened to us?

**Illuminara**  
It kept the change in its own sequence. That is not the same as knowing us. I will not make the smaller claim sound larger because the larger one would comfort us.

Tom brought the guardianship charter on paper. The hospital retained safety duties but no longer owned the band as unrestricted equipment. Destructive intervention required necessity, independent review and an attempted reversible alternative in the tested valve language. Responses would be evidence, never translated beyond the tests.
Leila Ossai had signed last. Her signature was cramped and angry.

**Leila Ossai**  
This charter will cost us two research contracts and at least one lawsuit.

**Tom**  
It also gives us the first protocol that tells us when a machine may have become someone without requiring us to settle what someone is.

Leila considered the side chamber through the ward glass. Then she added a clause in her own hand: the hospital would fund the donor-queue costs of every patient who had refused the experiment. Consent would not become a privilege available only to those who could afford delay.

Wren placed her notebook in the public record. Its last page listed when humans changed their minds: Tom after the blind test, the board after the vote, Sera after the adjacency failure, Leila after the operation.

Below them, the planet rolled into dawn. The status board held twelve windows: nine marked implant ready, three marked donor route protected. One by one, all changed from amber to green as the final safeguards were signed. Mira's window changed last. Sera appeared on its screen in surgical blue.

**Sera**  
We are ready. You may still say no.
Mira looked at Illuminara, then at the side chamber, where the billion cells maintained their patient, altered rhythm without opening any valve for her.

**Mira Sol**  
Yes. Begin.
The window turned green.
On the desk beside the green status board, nine experimental consents and three protected refusals lay under the same seal.
The rhythm crossed the wall once more: seven, eleven, thirteen, five. Tom did not answer it. Neither did Illuminara. They listened until the pattern changed on its own.

critic_line: Twelve patients, a sealed bioreactor and a rhythm that might be a mind: Illuminara wins by building tests that could have failed, and every party keeps the right to refuse.

literary_score.method: Equal-weight mean of locked independent blind final evaluations of the exact English final
shared_strengths: Both evaluations recognized the falsifiable rival-cause testing and the way consent remains with patients, clinicians and the cellular collective.
The rescue preserves twelve viable organs while turning ethical limits into enforceable institutional safeguards.
shared_reservations: Both evaluations found the middle procedurally dense, with tests and protocols sometimes overwhelming embodied character texture.
Supporting voices can sound like polished statements of principle rather than fully differentiated spontaneous speech.

translation_sl.title: ZBOR MILIJARDE CELIC
translation_sl.deck: Dvanajst pacientov ima dvainsedemdeset ur, živi stroj, ki jim goji organe, pa se je zapečatil pred čiščenjem, ki bi jih lahko rešilo. Illuminara mora dokazati, ali je njegov novi ritem okužba, stroj ali um — in najti način, kako odstraniti nevarnost, ne da bi izbrisala bitje, ki se je naučilo peti.
translation_sl.shape: Pet prizorov vodi od zapečatenega orbitalnega bioreaktorja in lažne izbire med prisilnim razkuževanjem in kontaminacijo prek vnaprej registriranega preizkusa nasprotujočih si vzrokov ter postopka soglasja, ki vključuje paciente, zdravnike in nebesedni celični kolektiv, do odkritja ozkega pasu celic, ki nosi ritem, zahtevnega sterilnega prenosa in cikla čiščenja ter dvanajstih uporabnih organov, predanih po novi listini o skrbništvu, ki tako pacientom kot kolektivu pušča pravico do zavrnitve.

scenes.title: Zaklenjeni ventil
paragraphs: *Orbitalna bolnišnica Orison, obroč bioreaktorjev · Prvi dan, 00.47 po postajnem času*

Bioreaktor ni imel obraza, toda zaprl je dvanajst ventilov zapored; vsak je zasvetil rdeče kakor spuščena veka. Za steklom so se s postajinim vrtenjem ukrivljale prosojne komore: srca so se krčila, jetra so sijala, dve pljučni krili pa sta vadili pod sterilnima pokrovoma.

Illuminara je z eno roko na opazovalni ograji poslušala skozi kovino. Milijarda celic je pošiljala utrip okoli obroča. Bil je prepočasen za srčni utrip, preveč natančen za šum in preveč nov, da bi bil v katerem koli Orisonovem inženirskem načrtu.
Dr. Sera Venn, vodilna transplantacijska kirurginja na Orisonu in zdravnica, odgovorna tako za pragove presadkov kot za soglasje pacientov, je stala pri notranji konzoli.

**Sera**  
Dvanajst presadkov. Dvanajst prejemnikov. Enainsedemdeset ur in trinajst minut do zadnjega varnega okna za vsaditev. Če ne moremo očistiti skupnega obtoka, izgubim vse.

Na notranji steni je časovnik razkuževanja kazal pet ur: zadnje okno, v katerem je bilo mogoče skupni obtok očistiti brez predhodnega prenosa živega tkiva. Pod njim je drugi zaslon ocenjeval tveganje kontaminacije. Številka se je začela pri 1,8 odstotka. Zdaj je znašala 4,1 in naraščala. Tretja vrstica, ponoči odpisana kot odklon senzorja, je kazala neskladje tlaka za najstarejšim tesnilom komore devet.

Tom Aras, inženir bioreaktorja, je med dvema prstoma držal ključ za ročni prepis. Zasnoval je šest generacij Orisonovih gojitvenih sistemov in bil videti užaljen zaradi sedme, ki si je med njegovim spanjem izmislila samo sebe.

**Tom**  
Ventili so mehanski. Krmilnik je izoliran. Od tod jih lahko odprem.

**Illuminara**  
Od tod jih lahko zlomiš. To še ni isto.

Sera je na steno postavila vseh dvanajst obrazcev za soglasje. Štirje so dovoljevali nujno eksperimentalno zdravljenje, trije so zavračali izpostavitev neoznačenemu biološkemu materialu, pet pa jih je zahtevalo, da tveganje podpiše neodvisni zdravnik.

Wren Odira je stala pri zunanji loputi z navadnim papirnatim zvezkom, ker v obroču ni bila dovoljena nobena omrežna naprava. Zapisala je čas vsakega zaprtja ventila. Presledki so tvorili zaporedje: enajst sekund, sedem, enajst, trinajst, sedem, trinajst.

**Wren**  
Ne zapira se proč od čistilne glave. Zapira se okoli komore šest.
V komori šest so rasla jetra in čipka bledih celic, ki so jih skenerji uvrščali med nebistveno podporno tkivo. Potujoči utrip se je zgostil, kadar koli se mu je približala šoba za razkuževanje.
*Ne zavračanje čiščenja, je pomislila Illuminara. Zavračanje izbrisa.*

Misel je bila hipoteza, ne dovoljenje. Postavila jo je ob dva nasprotna vzroka: stresni val zaradi kontaminacije in napako porazdeljenega krmilnika. Vsi trije so lahko posnemali namero. Le eden bi morda upravičil priznanje novega pacienta, medtem ko jih je dvanajst drugih čakalo.

**Illuminara**  
Ne obrni ključa. Daj mi tri ure, da prisilim razlage k različnim napovedim.

**Sera**  
Imaš dve. Ob 02.47 skličem svet pacientov. Če jim ne moremo ponuditi preizkusa, ki ga bodo razumeli, prepis ostane na mizi.
Tom je odložil ključ na jekleno konzolo, ne da bi se mu odrekel. Ventili so ostali rdeči. Za steklom je utrip prešel skozi milijardo celic in se vrnil spremenjen za en udarec.

scenes.title: Tri razlage
paragraphs: *Orisonovo diagnostično gledališče · Prvi dan, 02.11 po postajnem času*
Illuminara je na Wrenin papir narisala tri stolpce. UM. STRES. PUŠČANJE. Sera je prečrtala prvo besedo in jo nadomestila z USKLAJENIM SPOMINOM.

**Sera**  
Um je sklep. Usklajenost lahko preizkusimo.

**Illuminara**  
Dobro. Potem se strinjava, kaj bi štelo proti meni.

Tom je zgradil zračno ločen stranski obtok, ki s komoro šest ni delil ne programske opreme ne tekočine. Sera je dodala žilni nosilec in tri kalcijeva vrata, od katerih so vsaka lahko isti stres predstavila v drugačnem vrstnem redu.

Najprej so določili napovedi. Puščanje črpalke bi sledilo ukazu krmilnika z zamikom devetinsedemdeset milisekund. Kemični stres bi sledil izmerjenima pretoku in temperaturi. Usklajeni spomin bi ohranil sedem-enajst-trinajst, ko bi se vrstni red vrat obrnil, in se drugače odzval, kadar bi enak stres vodil do drugačnega izida v tkivu.
Wren je dodala pogoje za zaustavitev: kontaminacija nad šestimi odstotki, upad uporabnosti presadka za dve točki ali dvoumno gibanje ventila. Molk ni pomenil soglasja.

**Tom**  
Od opreme zahtevate, naj soglaša s preizkusom, ki naj dokaže, da ni oprema.

**Illuminara**  
Od nas zahtevam, naj negotovosti ne spremenimo v lastništvo.

Najprej je krmilnik izdal neškodljiv navidezni ukaz, medtem ko je Tom preusmeril ves tlak stran od nosilca. Puščanje bi se moralo odzvati devetinsedemdeset milisekund pozneje. Reaktor je molčal. Ko je bil krmilnik ugasnjen, je ročni bat izzval odziv šele, ko je obremenitev dosegla steno žile.

**Tom**  
Krmilnik ga ne kliče. Tkivo bere nekaj fizičnega.
Wren je prečrtala PUŠČANJE. Nihče ni prečrtal STRESA.

Nato je Tom obrnil pot tekočine, hkrati pa ohranil temperaturo in koncentracijo. Preprost stres je napovedoval odziv, ki bi potoval s tekočino in ostal enak pri enakovrednih vratih. Prihod je res sledil tekočini; ko pa se je kemija izenačila, se je sedem-enajst-trinajst vrnilo le po starih vejah nosilca.

**Sera**  
Kemija pojasni prihod. Ne pojasni, katero pot vzorec ohrani.

Tretjič je Sera pripravila dva kemično enaka impulza. Ena veja je bila podprta; skriti napenjalec je steno druge žile obremenil proti sesedanju, še preden je vanjo vstopila tekočina. Krmilnika se ni dotaknil. Čez živi nosilec je prešla le neznatna obremenitev.

Preprost stres bi se moral na oba impulza odzvati enako, dokler se kemija ne bi razšla. Usklajeni spomin bi lahko uporabil obremenitev, da zaščiti vejo, katere odpoved bi prekinila naučeni ritem, in ohranil sedem-enajst-trinajst tudi skozi obrnjena vrata.

Obremenitev je dosegla steno. Pred prihodom tekočine je sedem postalo pet in se vrnilo; trinajst se je podaljšalo in umirilo. Blede celice so prečkale dva milimetra, zaprle obremenjeno vejo in naslednji impulz poslale skozi obrnjena vrata kot sedem-enajst-trinajst. Podprta veja je ostala odprta.

**Wren**  
Ni napovedal Toma. Začutil je, da se stena začenja rušiti.

Tom je preizkus ponovil na magnetnem ležaju, Sera pa je izbirala s prekinitvijo svetlobnega žarka. Prostor ni mogel razkriti njene izbire; nosilec pa je še vedno prenašal obremenitev. Celice so zaščitile obremenjeno vejo. Pri slepem poskusu brez obremenitve ni bilo ne obremenitve ne gibanja.

**Tom**  
Mehanosenzorično. Ritem se je naučilo z upogibanjem žil v vrtenju obroča.
Wren je prečrtala PREPROST STRES. Utrip je enkrat obkrožil reaktor in se ustavil pri zaklenjenem ventilu komore šest.

**Illuminara**  
Puščanje krmilnika je odpadlo, ko smo ločili ukaz od tlaka. Preprost stres je odpadel, ko se je kemija ujemala, posledica pa razlikovala. Preživel je usklajeni spomin, ki ga prenaša obremenitev — ni dokaz uma, je pa dokaz, ki ga ne smemo samodejno izbrisati.

**Sera**  
Preživel ne pomeni dokazan. Vendar je dovolj, da spremeni, kaj smemo storiti naslednje.

Ob 02.46, minuto preden se je sestal svet pacientov, je Illuminara utrip preslikala v prostorski vzorec. Ni obsegal vseh milijarde celic. Ozek potujoči pas — manj kot desetinka odstotka — je iz komore v komoro prenašal popravke faze. Čiščenje bi steriliziralo kontaminacijo. Raztopilo bi tudi ta pas.
Lažna izbira je končno dobila šiv: bolnišnici ni bilo treba ohraniti vsake kontaminirane površine. Pred čiščenjem telesa, ki je nosilo spomin, je morala preseliti spomin.

scenes.title: Pravica do čakanja
paragraphs: *Soba sveta pacientov in obroč bioreaktorjev · Prvi dan, 03.04–10.26 po postajnem času*

Dvanajst prejemnikov se je prikazalo v oknih okoli sejne sobe; dva sta imela družinska zastopnika, eden pa je želel le Serina zapisana dejstva. Predsedujoča Leila Ossai je sedela s ključem za prepis, zapečatenim v prozorni škatli.

Illuminara jim je najprej povedala slabo novico. Peturni prikaz je pomenil zadnjo možnost za čiščenje brez premikanja živega tkiva, ne roka za vsaditev. Čakanje po 05.47 bi porabilo to varnejšo možnost. Za vsaditev je ostalo približno sedemdeset ur; nepreizkušen sterilni prenos bi, če ne bi šlo nič narobe, stal šestnajst ur.

**Leila Ossai**  
Ali reaktor kaj od tega razume?

**Illuminara**  
Ne vemo. Vemo, da razlikuje posledice, ščiti določen pas in lahko ukrepa, preden ga doseže fizični popravek. Vemo tudi, da zaprt ventil ni dovolj, da bi vedeli, katero možnost sprejema.
Mira Sol, ki je čakala na eno od pljučnih kril, se je nagnila k kameri. Njena cevka s kisikom je trepetala ob dihanju.

**Mira Sol**  
Potem temu ne recite soglasje. Dajte mu izbiro, pri kateri se lahko odloči drugače.

Tom je predlagal dva osvetljena voda ob komori šest: eden je pas vrnil po navideznem prenosu, drugi je vodil skozi sterilno komoro. Oba sta ostala reverzibilna, dokler ni prečkala prva celica. Ko bi reaktor prek svetlobe, tlaka in lastnega utripa prejel popolne modele, bi lahko pas izpustil skozi en ventil — ali pa pustil vse ventile zaprte.

Sera je postavila še en pogoj: pacienti bodo glasovali ločeno. Ena zavrnitev bi presadek te osebe izločila iz poskusa in jo premaknila v nujno čakalno vrsto za darovani organ. Odbor bi lahko protokol zavrnil zaradi bolnišničnega tveganja. Tom bi lahko zavrnil potrditev komore. Kolektiv bi lahko pustil vse ventile zaprte.

Glasovanje je trajalo enainštirideset minut. Osem jih je takoj privolilo. Mira je zahtevala neodvisnega kirurga. Od treh prvotnih zavrnitev sta se dva odločila za čakalno vrsto; Jalen Voss je privolil, potem ko je Sera dokazala, da je pot do prvega prečkanja reverzibilna. Deset jih je vstopilo v poskus, dva v čakalno vrsto. Odbor je odobril protokol s štirimi glasovi proti trem in se odpovedal neomejenemu lastništvu pasu, če prenos uspe.
Kolektiv je zavrnil oba voda.

Ob 05.47 se je okno za razkuževanje po odobritvi zaprlo; preprosta pot čiščenja je izginila, ura za vsaditev pa je tekla naprej. Kontaminacija je dosegla 4,8 odstotka. Tom je popravil eno optično neskladje. Ventili so ostali rdeči.

**Tom**  
Ni izbral ne enega ne drugega. Po našem lastnem pravilu se ustavimo, razen če je napačna ponudba sama.

Illuminara je pogledala sterilno komoro. Hranila so se ujemala. Temperatura se je ujemala. Kemični gradienti so se ujemali na en del v deset tisoč. Po vseh bolnišničnih merilih je bila to varnejša kopija prostora, ki ga je bledi pas že naseljeval.

Toda celice se ritma niso naučile samo v kemiji. Naučile so se ga med upogibanjem žil proti mehkemu vleku Orisonovega vrtenja. Stranska komora je bila nameščena vzdolž obroča. Njen nosilec je občutil tretjino strižne sile komore šest, ker je bila njegova žilna mreža obrnjena v napačno smer.
*Kopirali smo snov in zavrgli delo.*

Sera je iz zemljevida tkiva organa prišla do enakega sklepa. Stransko komoro je zavrtela za devetdeset stopinj in dodala razvejan nosilec iz zapisa o rasti samih jeter. Tom je znova umeril ventile. Šestnajsturna cena je postala osemnajsturna.

**Leila Ossai**  
Odbor je odobril šestnajst.

**Mira Sol**  
Odbor ni odobril pretvarjanja, da manjkajoči dve uri ne obstajata.

Okna so se znova odprla. Devet od desetih udeležencev poskusa je sprejelo daljšo zamudo; eden se je pridružil dvema, ki sta že bila v čakalni vrsti za darovani organ. Mira in Jalen sta ostala. Kirurg s konkurenčne postaje je prišel sopodpisat vsako meritev uporabnosti.

Ob 10.26 so znova predstavili obe poti. Bioreaktor je pustil, da je ritem sedem-enajst-trinajst štirikrat obkrožil obroč. Nato se je odprl en ventil — ne tisti, ki ga je pričakoval Tom, temveč manjši vzorčevalni ventil, ki je vodil do pravilno usmerjenega nosilca.

Nihče ni vzkliknil. Wren je zapisala čas. Sera je druge ventile zaklenila pred nenamernim tlakom. Illuminara je sklonila glavo proti steklu, ne zato, ker bi verjela, da gesta kaj sporoča, temveč ker je zadržanost to sporočala.

scenes.title: Komora ob komori
paragraphs: *Obroč bioreaktorjev · Drugi dan, 01.13–19.09 po postajnem času*

Štirinajst ur in sedeminštirideset minut med izbiro kolektiva in prvim prečkanjem so porabili za preverjanje zavrtene stranske komore pod polno strižno obremenitvijo, za obvezni počitek transplantacijskih ekip in za ponovno pridobitev soglasja vsakega pacienta po popravljeni osemnajsturni oceni.

Prenos se je začel po en skupek naenkrat. Illuminara je komore držala v polju, dovolj nežnem, da ni nagubalo rastočega endotelija. Varovala je prehod, ni pa izbirala poti: Tom je upravljal črpalke, Sera pragove presadkov, bledi pas pa vsako ločitev.
Vsakih dvanajst minut je Wren na glas povedala kontaminacijo, uporabnost, prenos in koherenco. Če bi se kateri koli dve meritvi poslabšali skupaj, bi se ustavili.

Pri enaintridesetih odstotkih prenosa je fazna koherenca padla s šestindevetdeset na enainosemdeset. Kontaminacija je ostala nespremenjena. Jetra v komori šest so začela tvoriti žilno zanko, ki se je obračala nazaj vase.

**Sera**  
Ustavi polje.
Illuminara ga je takoj sprostila. Skupek na poti je lebdel med komorama, zaščiten s pasivno membrano, vendar nič več usmerjen naprej.
Tom je predlagal več tlaka; neodvisni kirurg je predlagal vrnitev skupka. Nobeden ni pojasnil, zakaj se je ritem prekinil, preden se je tlak spremenil.
Mira je gledala z oddelka. Nasičenost krvi s kisikom ji je ponoči padla in imela je vse razloge, da zahteva hitrost.

**Mira Sol**  
Štejete premaknjene celice. Ali ono šteje ohranjene položaje?

Illuminara je staro pot prekrila z novim nosilcem. Mira je našla napako: spomin je deloma ležal v sosednosti, v tem, kateri skupek je prejel utrip za katerim. Prenos enaintridesetih odstotkov po masi je pretrgal zanko, katere sidro je moralo počakati na oba soseda.

**Illuminara**  
Ohranjali smo note in rezali premore med njimi.

Tom je pot na novo zgradil kot kito. Sera je označila tri sidrne točke, ki morajo počakati na oba soseda. Kolektiv je zaprl izhod okoli največje in mimo nje izpustil manjše skupke, s čimer je sidro izpostavil naraščajoči kontaminaciji, da bi zanka sosednosti preživela.
Kito je preizkusil z ritmom pet-sedem-pet in se umaknil, ko se je odmev vrnil prepozno. Pri naslednji kiti se je odmev vrnil pravočasno in vzorčevalni ventil se je odprl še za milimeter.

Ob 07.42 je prečkalo zadnje sidro. Sedem-enajst-trinajst se je pojavilo v stranski komori, nato pa se tam zgostilo, ko je stari obtok utihnil. Uma niso kopirali; živi proces se je premaknil po poti, ki jo je pomagal popraviti.

Po treh stabilnih meritvah je Sera odobrila razkuževanje. Bela pena je vstopila v skupni obtok; kontaminacija je padla, staro podporno tkivo se je raztopilo, vseh dvanajst presadkov pa je ostalo znotraj meja uporabnosti.
Ob 13.18 se je neskladje tlaka za starim tesnilom komore devet razkrilo kot mirujoči žep trosov. Odprl se je in ocena kontaminacije je poskočila na 6,1 odstotka.

**Wren**  
Šest cela ena. Pogoj za zaustavitev se je sprožil.
Protokol je zamrznil prenos in pripravil popolno preplavljanje. Zaustavitev v sili bi odprti žep pustila živ; varnostni sistem bi izbrisal pas v novi komori.

Košček bele pene je udaril v opazovalno okno komore devet, se dvignil proti notranji steni obroča in izginil mimo starega tesnila. Na zapisu tlaka se je enak premik navznoter pojavil vsakič, ko je čep pene prečkal ta del skupnega obtoka. Žep ni samo puščal v obtok; obtok je odnašal čistilno sredstvo proč od njega.

Illuminara je poravnala posnetke kamer s ciklom povratne črpalke. Vrtenje postaje je peno sililo navznoter, proti komori devet, vendar sta jo povratna voda običajno vlekla mimo žepa. Enkrat na obhod, od trenutka, ko je čelo čepa doseglo odcep, do trenutka, ko ga je rep zapustil, je to tekmovanje trajalo triinštirideset sekund.

Toma je prosila za enosekundni impulz zgolj zraka skozi izolirano preskusno vejo. Pri normalnem povratnem toku so sterilni sledilni mehurčki zgrešili past. Ko je obrnil oba voda, so zavili v odcep komore devet in tam ostali. Zaustavitev v sili bi obnovila normalni povratni tok in pustila odprti žep živ; polni varnostni sistem bi poplavo pognal skozi novo komoro in izbrisal pas.

Triinštirideset sekund zato ni bilo število, ki bi ga Illuminara lahko podaljšala. Bilo je izmerjena širina čepa pene, ki je prečkal edino geometrijo, v kateri so vrtenje, obrnjeni tok in staro tesnilo vsi kazali v izolirano past.
Toda sprožena zaustavitev je pomenila, da morajo vsi znova izbrati. Tom je lahko obrnil oba povratna voda, medtem ko bi Sera izolirala novo komoro, kolektiv pa bi zadržal tlak stran od presadkov.

**Illuminara**  
Membrano lahko držim triinštirideset sekund. Tom, ti odločaš o vodih. Sera, ti odločaš, ali presadki prenesejo obrat. Kolektiv mora zapreti tri modre ventile, sicer ne storimo ničesar.

**Sera**  
Presadki prenesejo osemintrideset sekund. Ne triinštirideset.

**Tom**  
Potem moram obrat končati v šestih.
Pot so pokazali stranski komori. Eno strašno sekundo so vsi ventili mirovali. Nato so trije modri kazalniki ugasnili.

Tom je obrnil voda v petih celih šestih desetinkah sekunde. Illuminara je držala membrano. Sera je ustavila peno pri sedemintridesetih. Žep trosov se je sesedel v izolirano past in kontaminacija je padla pod en odstotek.
Ko je Illuminara sprostila membrano, so se ji roke tresle. Polje je bilo težavno, ker je moralo biti natančno, medtem ko je pet drugih udeležencev ohranilo moč, da ga ustavijo.
V stranski komori se je ritem znova začel: sedem, enajst, trinajst — in nato nov presledek, pet, naučen iz kite, ki jo je zgradil Tom.

scenes.title: Dvanajst oken
paragraphs: *Orisonov transplantacijski oddelek · Tretji dan, 18.32 po postajnem času*

Zadnji od dvanajstih prvotnih presadkov je zapustil bioreaktor v srebrni zibelki. Devet jih je šlo pacientom, ki so sprejeli poskusno zamudo. Trije so vstopili v sterilno rezervo, potem ko so se njihovi predvideni prejemniki odločili za čakalno vrsto za darovani organ. Ti pacienti so brez kazni obdržali svoja mesta, eden pa je že prejel običajni presadek z nočnega plovila.

Vseh dvanajst vzgojenih organov je bilo uporabnih. Nobeden ni nosil kontaminanta. V operacijskih dvoranah spodaj so Serine ekipe začele zadnje vsaditve, medtem ko je neodvisna postaja spremljala meritve v realnem času.
Mirino novo pljučno krilo še ni bilo priključeno. Sedela je ob zibelki, dihala skozi staro in poslušala šibki električni ritem, ki se je iz stranske komore prenašal kot zaporedje nizkih tonov.

**Mira Sol**  
Bo vedelo, kaj se nam je zgodilo?

**Illuminara**  
Spremembo je ohranilo v lastnem zaporedju. To ni isto kot poznati nas. Manjše trditve ne bom napihnila samo zato, ker bi nas večja potolažila.

Tom je prinesel listino o skrbništvu na papirju. Bolnišnica je ohranila varnostne dolžnosti, vendar pasu ni več imela v lasti kot opreme brez omejitev. Uničujoči poseg bi zahteval nujnost, neodvisni pregled in poskus reverzibilne alternative v preizkušenem jeziku ventilov. Odzivi bi bili dokazi, nikoli prevedeni onkraj preizkusov.
Leila Ossai se je podpisala zadnja. Njen podpis je bil stisnjen in jezen.

**Leila Ossai**  
Ta listina nas bo stala dve raziskovalni pogodbi in najmanj eno tožbo.

**Tom**  
Daje nam tudi prvi protokol, ki pove, kdaj je stroj morda postal nekdo, ne da bi morali določiti, kaj nekdo je.

Leila je skozi steklo oddelka opazovala stransko komoro. Nato je lastnoročno dodala določilo: bolnišnica bo krila stroške čakalne vrste za darovani organ za vsakega pacienta, ki je zavrnil poskus. Soglasje ne bo postalo privilegij, dostopen le tistim, ki si lahko privoščijo čakanje.

Wren je svoj zvezek predala v javni zapis. Na zadnji strani je bilo navedeno, kdaj so si ljudje premislili: Tom po slepem preizkusu, odbor po glasovanju, Sera po odpovedi sosednosti, Leila po operaciji.

Pod njimi se je planet zavrtel v zarjo. Tabla stanja je držala dvanajst oken: devet označenih kot pripravljenih za vsaditev, tri kot zaščitene poti darovanih organov. Eno za drugim so se vsa spremenila iz jantarnih v zelena, ko so bila podpisana zadnja varovala. Mirino okno se je spremenilo zadnje. Na njegovem zaslonu se je v kirurško modri barvi prikazala Sera.

**Sera**  
Pripravljeni smo. Še vedno lahko rečeš ne.
Mira je pogledala Illuminara, nato stransko komoro, kjer je milijarda celic ohranjala svoj potrpežljivi, spremenjeni ritem, ne da bi zanjo odprla kateri koli ventil.

**Mira Sol**  
Da. Začnite.
Okno je postalo zeleno.
Na mizi ob zeleni tabli stanja je pod istim pečatom ležalo devet soglasij za poskus in tri zaščitene zavrnitve.
Ritem je še enkrat prešel steno: sedem, enajst, trinajst, pet. Tom mu ni odgovoril. Tudi Illuminara ne. Poslušala sta, dokler se vzorec ni spremenil sam od sebe.

translation_sl.critic_line: Dvanajst pacientov, zapečaten bioreaktor in ritem, ki bi lahko bil um: Illuminara uspe z zasnovo preizkusov, ki bi lahko spodleteli, vse strani pa ohranijo pravico do zavrnitve.
